title: Taisho Girl Fairy Tale
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In Taisho-era Japan, Tamahiko Shima, son of a wealthy family, loses his mother and the use of his right hand in an accident, and his father, ashamed, sends him to a countryside villa and has him declared legally dead. Bitter and withdrawn, Tamahiko expects to waste away, until Yuzuki, a cheerful girl sold to the family to settle her family's debts, arrives as his bride-to-be and helper. Her warmth and the villagers they befriend slowly draw him back into life (MANGA MILLION blurb; MU desc; ANN review of the anime adaptation).
life_message: Patient, cheerful love and a caring community can heal a person the world has written off.

content.note: Father's abuse of Tamahiko and his sister; an alcoholic father neglects village children (ANN review; MU Abusive Parent/s).
Accident and mother's death in backstory; an earthquake later (MU Earthquake) (to verify).
A 14-year-old girl sold as a bride-to-be; romance is chaste in the anime per ANN, but MU tags Big Breasts and MangaDex rates it suggestive (to verify).
Tamahiko's depression and resignation to a 'living death'; suicidal thoughts tagged (ANN review; MU Depression, Suicidal Character/s; AniList Hikikomori).
A child bride bought to settle debt presented as a fairy tale (ANN; MU Arranged Marriage).

Dignity vs honor.evidence: Father hides his son to avoid family shame; the son's worth is restored by love.

Order vs freedom.evidence: Characters accept arranged roles and household duties.

Civic vs kin.evidence: Family obligation, debt and marriage drive everything; villagers become kin.

Equality vs hierarchy.evidence: Patriarchal father's authority; wealthy heir and purchased bride.

folkways.japan: Taisho-era (1912-1926) family customs, arranged marriage to settle debt and household shame over disability reflect historical Japanese norms.

delivery.evidence: ANN review of the anime says kindness resolves problems too easily and Yuzuki lacks inner complexity.

personified.ideology: family honor over a disabled son

delivery.note: The reviewer notes trauma explains how hurt people hurt others, though the story leans on Yuzuki's sunniness.

winners_losers: Tamahiko and Yuzuki build a happy household; the cold, abusive father is the story's failure. Sympathy goes to gentle devotion.
